preamble: Click loss in East Kalahari Khoe (Shua and Tshwa clusters: Cara, ǀXaise, Danisi, Deti, Kua, Tsua). Here the palatal click series of Proto-Kalahari Khoe has been largely replaced, mostly by non-click palatal consonants (Tsua and southern Kua still keep some palatal clicks), a regular sound change documented by Traill & Vossen (1997). Sands & Gunnink (2019) note that Khoe click loss increases with distance from the Kalahari core and may be sped up by contact with languages that lack clicks. Western languages such as ǀGwi and Kxoe, and Ts'ixa, which often has the click (partly through contact with Kxoe), keep it, e.g. ǀGwi ǂéē (Nakagawa 2006), Ts'ixa ǂé 'ear'. In Kua and Tsua, the plain palatal click before non-high vowels (e, a/o) became a palatalized velar [kʲ], where the other East Kalahari varieties have [tɕ]. Before u and in *ǂx, Kua and Tsua also have tɕ (ɕúì 'nose', ɕxàí 'eye'). Both examples are core vocabulary from a single source (Vossen 1997, via the GLD). Forms follow the GLD's transcription (Vossen 1997 data). In that system ɕ and ʓ are palatal (alveolo-palatal) affricates [tɕ, dʑ], y is [j], and ʸ marks palatalization.
